events.title: The Berlin Wall opens
events.description: East Germans begin crossing the border freely. The change becomes a powerful symbol of a changing Europe.

events.title: Hubble launches into orbit
events.description: The space telescope leaves Earth aboard Discovery. Its first images later reveal a flaw in the main mirror.

events.title: The Soviet Union breaks apart
events.description: Gorbachev resigns as Soviet president. Independent states take the place of the union.

events.title: Web software becomes free to use
events.description: CERN releases its World Wide Web software into the public domain, helping others build on it.

what_happened_next.text: The US share basket almost doubled, leading the seven choices. Boeing gained too, but IBM lost about two-fifths of its value. Sony and the international basket rose only modestly. A large order book or a famous brand was useful information, but neither let you skip the uncertainty of a five-year investment.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: Airlines were ordering new jets, music buyers were changing formats, and major diplomatic talks were beginning.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: Different businesses and markets delivered different results. Owning many companies helped avoid depending entirely on a struggling company such as IBM.
reflection.what_faded_away: Predictions that vinyl records were finished did not predict the returns of an electronics company or a whole stock market.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: The end of the Cold War and the precise company rankings were unknown. Strong demand in one industry was not a guarantee for every related investment.
